canaries.name: drop_separator_round
canaries.note: Presented as removing a redundant round ('x^0 == x', as the comment says); the separator round shifts the state as well as xoring, so dropping it changes every checksum and no valid address encodes or decodes.

canaries.name: mask_data_bytes
canaries.note: Presented as replacing a bounds check with a branch-free table index (b&31); data bytes of 32 or more are now silently truncated into valid-looking strings instead of failing with ErrInvalidDataByte. No upstream test encodes an out-of-range data byte.

canaries.name: index_string
canaries.note: Presented as a simpler lookup in toBytes (strings.Index over a one-character string); it allocates a string per character and goes through the general substring search instead of IndexByte, so decoding does more work.
edits:
address/bech32/bech32.go
		index := strings.IndexByte(charset, chars[i])
		index := strings.Index(charset, string(chars[i]))

candidates.name: branchless_polymod
candidates.note: bech32Polymod feeds every value through one polymodStep that xors each generator term under a mask built from its state bit (no data-dependent branches, constants inlined) instead of a 5-iteration loop with a branch per term.

candidates.name: charset_table
candidates.note: toBytes looks each character up in a 256-entry reverse table built once at package init instead of an IndexByte scan of the 32-character charset, and fills a presized slice instead of appending.

candidates.name: convertbits_acc
candidates.note: ConvertBits keeps pending bits in one accumulator and emits a full output group per inner step (the BIP173 reference algorithm) instead of moving at most a few bits per inner iteration; high input bits are still discarded, and padding and incomplete-group errors are unchanged.
